description:
Defining a repository gate re-renders `.jit/reference/rules-and-gates.md`, which the sim-research profile claims, so every gate addition breaks `jit validate` until someone re-records the profile fingerprint by hand.

## Background

The projection lists every gate in the registry. The profile owns the rendered file but only some of its content: 19 of the repository's 24 gates are profile contributions, and five — `f3-bipedal-ci`, `gf2-kernels-hip-ci`, `permanent-sampling-feas-ci`, `permanent-wave-gpu-ci`, and `research-review` — are repository-local. Adding one is ordinary work, but it moves a file the profile claims, and `jit validate` then fails with `[profile-ownership] '.jit/reference/rules-and-gates.md' no longer holds the value this profile published`. Because `repo-validate` is itself a gate, the red state propagates to any issue carrying it.

Two further inconsistencies sit behind this:

- The package's published copy at `packages/sim-research/assets/install/.jit/reference/rules-and-gates.md` names six gates — `breakdown-review`, `code-review`, `coverage-preview`, `jit-validate`, `plan-review`, `repo-validate` — while the repository copy names all 24. It also describes `breakdown-review` and `plan-review` as external-review placeholders, where the repository defines both as automated `ai-review.sh` checkers. The published asset and the live repository file describe different registries.
- `manifest.toml` declares that file both as an install-only `[[asset]]` and beneath the `.jit/reference` `[[live-source]]` root. The asset declaration wins, so `jit profile capture` reads the package's own copy and reports no change; the error message's suggested capture is a no-op against this drift.

The immediate breakage is repaired by `jit profile reconfigure`, which re-records the claim fingerprint without changing any file. That repair is manual and must be repeated after every gate change.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Adding a gate to the registry and rendering the projections leaves `jit validate` green with no manual profile re-record.
- [hard] REQ-02: The published package asset and the repository's rendered projection no longer describe different gate sets, or the package no longer publishes that file at all.
- [hard] REQ-03: `.jit/reference/rules-and-gates.md` is declared once in `manifest.toml`, so `jit profile capture` and the ownership check draw the file's authoritative content from the same place.
- [hard] REQ-04: The chosen resolution is recorded with the reasoning, including what a fresh install of the profile publishes for this file afterwards.

## Notes

Removing a gate is the mirror case and should be checked the same way as REQ-01.
title: Gate additions break profile-ownership validation of the rules-and-gates projection
